reason: Both conversations correctly identified the whirr as the normal cooling fan, asked sensible questions about hob type and noise character, and reassured the worried homeowner without recommending parts or an engineer. Conversation 1 edged ahead with more accurate detail (2-10 minute run-on matching the customer's 'few minutes', versus Conversation 2's '10-20 minutes' and an overly lenient 'continues for hours' escalation threshold), clearer red flags (grinding noise, self-switch-off, scorch marks) and practical advice about not blocking airflow or cutting power at the wall mid-cooldown. Its opening reply was over-broad, covering gas and ceramic hobs the customer didn't have, which is why the margin is only slight rather than clear.
